proofs.statement: Lemma A1/A2 (window form): S2 holds iff, for some t in T, S_{n+4}(t) = Phi(L+r-t) - Phi(L+2r+t) - psi(t) is negative. Here n=N*, L=(n+2)r/2, Phi(w)=sum_{i>=0} e(w+ir), and psi is the class-sum profile. Every binding window has the form V_b(t) = H((b+1)r/2,t) - psi(t) with H(w,t)=Phi(w-t)-Phi(w+t).

Theorem B* (cross-pair transfer). Assume (H2): for z >= L - r/2, e(z+1) <= e^{-kappa/r} e(z). Let lambda >= max_t psi(t)/t, and assume (K*): some t1 in T has 2(1-e^{-kappa})^2 psi(t1) >= lambda r e^{-kappa(1-t1/r)}. Then a binding pair anywhere forces a negative (N*+4)-window centred at t1+r/2, so beta <= N*+2. Theorem B (sine form) and Corollary C2 give a residue-level certificate eps = sum_{j>=2} j|beta_j|/beta_1 < 1, where beta_j is computed from R_j = prod_i sin(pi j a_i/r)/sin(pi j/r).

Proposition D (obstruction). S2 does not follow from the framework's qualitative ingredients: palindromic log-concave A, Lemma 2.1, the sign lemma, cyclic unimodality of Gamma, and sum tau = 0. Explicit sequences D1-D3 satisfy all of these but violate S2, so no cross-pair inequality built only from them can prove S2.

proofs.statement: Lemma 1: TP_rho holds for every residue multiset rho. If Q_z<0, then d_y<0 with y=sigma+1-r-z, so 2y>sigma+1 and d_y>=tau_y, hence tau_y<0. By T11 Lemma 7 together with tau_{sigma+1-t}=-tau_t, floor((2y-sigma-1)/r) is then even.

Lemma 2: E_rho holds for every rho, and in fact ND_rho(K_j) holds for every even j>=0 with no lower bound on K. Each such window sum, centred in (0,r/2], is an alternating sum A_j of a nonnegative unimodal sequence whose total is a class sum tau_{t0}>=0 by cyclic unimodality.

Lemma 3: O_rho <=> r(N*(rho)+5) > sigma+1-2mu*_inf, where N*(rho) is the least odd j with ND_rho(K_j) false. For odd j, ND_rho(K_j) <=> P_{j+1}(rho) unimodal. Equivalently, O_rho <=> N*(rho) >= floor((sigma+1-2mu*_inf)/r)-3, and the slack is always <=3 and odd. Corollary 5: if r(N*(rho)+5) > sigma+1-2mu*_inf(k,tau), then S2 holds for every a with residue multiset rho.

Proposition 4: O_rho is false in general. There is an explicit fit-box counterexample (r=57, k=52) and a general mechanism. Adding parts equal to 1 leaves A_rho, sigma, tau, ND and N*(rho) unchanged but lowers mu*_inf down to mu_neg once binom(k,2)>=max tau. The certificate then becomes the strong one, which is known to fail (for example r=30, 14-part rho', for any m>=133,084 ones).

failure_report:
The path cannot be completed, because the target statement 'TP_rho, E_rho, O_rho hold for every rho' is false.

What works (proved in /tmp/claude-0/qu/explore3/R3E2/proof_TPE.txt):
- TP_rho holds for every rho, by cyclic unimodality (T11 Lemma 7) plus e>=0 on the lower half.
- E_rho holds for every rho, even without the lower bound K>=2mu*_inf. It is the automatic half: alternating sums of a nonnegative unimodal sequence whose total is a class sum >=0.
- O_rho is equivalent to one inequality: r(N*(rho)+5) > sigma+1-2mu*_inf(k,tau). Equivalently N*(rho) >= floor((sigma+1-2mu*_inf)/r)-3, and the slack is always 1 or 3 when O holds. So Theorem R reduces to that single inequality (Corollary 5).

Where it breaks: O_rho is false.
- Explicit fit-box counterexample: r=57, rho=(1^37,6,7,9,15,18,20,22,23,25,26,27,28,30,33,37), k=52, sigma=311. P_2(rho) is not unimodal, so N*=1 and K_1=141. mu*_inf=-16, so 2mu*_inf+3r=139<=141 and O fails. With 36 ones it holds (mu*_inf=14).
- More cases with minimal padding m (number of ones): m=64 (r=50), m=73 (r=31), m=58 (r=28), m=98 (r=21).
- 44 of 137 random padded rho' (k=140) fail O.
- Without residue-1 parts, O held in 1500 of 1500 cases; with few ones, in 2893 of 2893.

Mechanism (proved): ones change only k, hence f, hence mu*_inf, which drops toward mu_neg >= -r. Meanwhile N*(rho) and mu*(rho) stay fixed. Once binom(k,2)>=max tau, O becomes the strong certificate O+, which is known to fail (R2E2: 25,737 rho').

The failure is in the certificate, not in S2. Lifts of the counterexample have U=[1,40]u{42}, [1,55]u{57}, [1,144]u{146}, [1,300]u{302}, and ND_a(K_1) holds for each. Lifting strictly improves ND, and the residue level loses this.

Consequence: any certificate of this kind fails on rho padded with ones. That covers residue-level ND together with any lower bound on mu*(a) that is uniform over all lifts. The k-dependence through mu*_inf runs the wrong way.

proofs.statement:
THEOREM: Conjecture S2 holds for r=4, r=5 and r=6, for every k and every part sizes. If r divides no a_i, then U = [1,B*] or [1,B*]\{B*-1}.

Uses (cited as refereed): the round-2 synthesis (Thms 3.1 and 4.2, Lemmas 2.1, 3.2, 3.3, 4.1), R2E2 Theorem R (the reduction only; I did not use the R2E2 certificate run, every residue certificate here is my own recomputation), and Thm E.

Proof structure.
(1) Lemma 1 (new): if L' := y_{n+1}-y_{n+2} >= y_{n+4} holds at n=n*(C) for every class pair C with A_inf != 0, then beta_C <= n*(C)+2 for every pair, and S2 follows.
(2) The y-sequence is nonincreasing after n*. The crossing satisfies T_{n*+1} < |A_inf|.
(3) Explicit bounds V on |A_inf| from roots of unity: r=4 gives 2^floor((n2-1)/2); r=5 gives about 0.47 phi^k; r=6 gives 3^{p/2}2^s/3+1.
(4) Operator lemmas for products of q-integers (L_n=(1+q)d/dq-n, P_n=n-(1-q)d/dq), which give:
  - two-sided ratio bounds j/(j+k-1) <= alpha_{j-1}/alpha_j <= j/(k-j+1);
  - alpha_j/C(k,j) is nondecreasing and convex, hence second-difference bounds;
  - binomial and trinomial domination.
(5) A covering criterion: at each candidate crossing position, either L' holds by the bounds, or T >= V, which rules the position out.
(6) Assembly by cases:
  - r=4: exhaustive exact-tail check for k<=15; analytic certificate for 12<=k<=140; hand proof for k>=141. This case does not use Theorem R.
  - r=5: own residue certificate plus Theorem R for k<=23, with the fit-box-excluded classes covered analytically using V<=5; analytic certificate for 24<=k<=140; hand proof for k>=141.
  - r=6: own residue certificate plus Theorem R for k<=53, with the excluded classes covered using V<=11; two-parameter analytic certificate for 54<=k<=140; hand proof (entropy and Robbins/Stirling bounds) for k>=141.

All numeric certificates use only k<=140 and instances inside the fit box.

Caveat on the path. The asymptotic regime runs through the class-pair inequality L', not the residue-level TP/E/O conditions, because the residue-level asymptotics fail: 179 of 2,998 rho' fail for r=4. A side effect: in the regimes handled by Lemma 1, the pair-local inequality beta_C <= n*(C)+2 is proved. For r=5 with k<=23 and r=6 with k<=53, the proof uses Theorem R instead.

It predicts excess = gap - 2 = 2*min_w[(ln(pi(1-e^-kappa)/kappa) - ln sin(pi w))/kappa + w/2]. Excess is in index units; failure needs excess >= 2. Observed mean excess 0.065 against model mean 0.068 (n=1602, r >= 3000, N* >= 5, correlation 0.52). Observed maximum 0.30, reached by k=5 lifted instances. failure_report:
I found no counterexample to S2. Every instance I evaluated (316,601 evaluations, all with r >= 1000, up to r = 50000) has beta - N* in {0, 2}. A global S2 failure needs beta - N* >= 4.

Measures I used:
- gap = umin - vmin, the continuous crossing positions of the two threshold sequences T_{n+1} and T_{b-1}+y_b, in index units. A failure needs gap >= 4. In well-resolved instances the gap stays at 2.0-2.34. The baseline of 2 is structural.
- The failure margin min_C log((T_{N*+3}+y_{N*+4})/|A_C|), which must be >= 0. The best value is -1.135 levels, about -6.8 nats.
- Exact checks: the two best new near-misses were verified by brute force and by the exact pair criterion (verify_nearmiss.py).

Why it fails (heuristic, quantitative, not a proof):
- In level units with decay kappa per r-step, pair C has beta_C ~ 2*floor(u_C)+1 and n*(C) ~ 2*floor(u_C - delta_C)+1. Here u_C = -ln|tau(t_C)|/kappa - C/(2r), and delta_C ~ ln((1-e^-kappa)/(1-e^{-kappa(r-C)/r}))/kappa is large only for small-gap pairs, C near r.
- A global failure needs min_C u_C >= min_C(u_C - delta_C) + 1.
- Antisymmetry forces tau to vanish at the anti-centre class C = r. So |tau| grows linearly in g' = r-C there, and this cancels the delta advantage of the small-gap pairs to first order.
- With a sinusoidal tau the excess is only about 0.07 levels at kappa ~ 5-6. This matches the data (mean 0.065 vs 0.068).
- Escaping needs either kappa < ~1, or a tau concentrated within about r e^{-kappa}/kappa classes of the anti-centre.

Neither is reachable:
- kappa: the binomial-tail (lifted) regime gives kappa >~ pi*e*(1-2/k). The Gaussian regime gives kappa >= 2*pi. The smallest resolved kappa found by a dedicated minimisation (hc4) and in the surveys was about 3.9.
- Concentrated tau: this needs many comparable harmonics. That happens only with small effective residues (s or r-s, with s << r). These make |tau| tiny, push the crossing to the extreme tail, and make kappa about e*r/s, which is huge.
- The designed family built on exactly this idea (two residues near r/2 for a triangle-wave Gamma, small-width parts, lifted +-1 parts; 216 instances) gives beta = N* in every case, with margin -50.

Closest near-misses:
- r=15167, k=111 (the r2 instance): margin -1.135 levels.
- r=5000, k=150, a_i in [1394,1493]: margin -1.19 levels; exact U contains 9,10,11 and is not unimodal at b = 12..16 (b = 1..8 not checked).
- r=8000, a=(12871,12875,12921,20863,20986): largest resolved excess, 0.30 index units; exact U contains 6,7,8 and is not unimodal at b = 9..13 (b = 1..5 not checked).
A failure needs about +1 level of margin, i.e. excess >= 2.

Limits:
- The search was in floating point. Ties, if any, would need exact rechecks, but no instance came within a level of failing.
- Hill-climbs at r >= 10000 were slow, 1.6k-5k evaluations per run.
- I did not search r > 50000 exhaustively. The model says larger r only helps pair-local failures (r >~ kappa e^kappa), not the global inequality.
- Coarsely sampled instances (D/r small) give gap values up to 3.69, but these are interpolation artifacts; in all of them beta = N*.
